factProposals.value: Draft reviews call Claude (claude-sonnet-5) through the official Anthropic Python SDK, with the key read from the git-ignored .env; one request per rule stage with structured JSON output.

An AI evaluation returns the rule ids that pass plus FAIL or ADVISORY findings, each with rule id, severity, evidence, reason, suggested student feedback and a confidence score; it has no approval or status field.
ADVISORY marks a rule the AI cannot judge from the text (for example what a screenshot shows or whether a link opens); the human reviewer checks it.

Students mark the selected problem with a yellow highlight stored in two forms: an inline style background-color: rgb(250, 247, 133) (12 of 45 ST0 critique comments in the history) and Basecamp's newer <mark style="background-color: var(--highlight-bg-1)"> (8 of 45).

Most ST0 submissions list their Data Science problems as blocks of labelled fields without numbering: counting 'Problem N' finds a count in 12 of 45 historical critique comments, counting the required field labels in 36 of 45.
Students often paste the dataset URL as plain text rather than as a Basecamp link (2 of the 15 ST0 comparison cases).

Reviewers sometimes write '##Critique##' inside their own feedback comments together with ##FeedbackGiven## or ##Approved## (13 of 553 critique detections in the history extract), and sometimes post a bare ##Critique## themselves.
After the reviewer's ##FeedbackGiven## the thread continues: the student posts an updated version with a new ##Critique##, and that version should be reviewed against the feedback given last time.
Some submissions put their content only in an attached Word document; the evaluator cannot read it and such a submission currently gets FAIL on every rule.

AI evaluation cost is bounded by a per-call output cap, a manual-resolution threshold on input tokens and a daily token limit from the environment; 15 historical ST0 submissions cost $0.26 in total with Claude Sonnet 5 at low effort.
Tests remove every Anthropic credential source so no test can reach the paid API; the evaluation scripts read the project .env over the shell so another project's key is never used.

decisions.statement: Evaluate with claude-sonnet-5 at low effort, using a cached system prompt built only from the rule module, plain text with [SELECTED] markers, deterministic pre-checks, structured output and a pass list instead of PASS findings.
Stage order is applied in code: Stage 2 is only requested after a Stage 1 answer with no FAIL.
decisions.rationale: the ST0 spec says a Stage 1 failure stops the review; code is deterministic, a model instruction is not, and it saves a call

decisions.statement: Severity on a finding is taken from the rule module, not from Claude's answer, and an answer that misses or adds rule ids is rejected.
decisions.rationale: rules and severities are versioned configuration; the model must not change them

decisions.statement: An evaluation is idempotent on (comment_id, rule_version); only a stored success blocks a later Claude call, and the result is stored before the finding/completed audit events.
decisions.rationale: user decision; storing first means an audit failure never costs a second paid call

decisions.statement: The SDK's automatic retries are off; the client retries at most twice with Retry-After capped at 30 seconds.
decisions.rationale: the SDK honours any Retry-After however long, which would break the no-unbounded-waits rule

decisions.statement: Evaluation results, the usage ledger and locks are git-ignored JSON Lines files, not SQL Server tables.
A comment carrying ##Critique## together with ##FeedbackGiven## or ##Approved## is treated as reviewer feedback: the intake does not queue it and the evaluator refuses it.
decisions.rationale: user-approved fix after the historical comparison graded reviewer comments as submissions

decisions.statement: Previous feedback on the same thread is looked up exactly by thread id; the vector database (STORY-013) is kept for finding similar cases from other students.
decisions.rationale: agreed with the user: an exact lookup cannot mix students up and costs nothing; similarity search is what a vector database is for

limitations.statement: Reviewer notes from the rule module (CONTENT_NOT_IN_TEXT, SPLIT_SUBMISSION) are not produced yet.
The evaluator reads only the reviewed comment; previous versions and the reviewer's previous feedback are not yet passed to Claude (the thread reader is built but not wired in).
A call that times out reports no token usage, so the daily usage ledger can undercount.
A reviewer who posts a bare ##Critique## with no other marker is still queued as a submission; telling reviewers from students needs the critiquer list.
Agreement with human feedback is measured by keyword hints only; the reviewer must read the side-by-side report to judge it.
